issue.body:
Fixes #196508

## What Problem This Solves

`writeDreamsFileAtomic` always publishes DREAMS.md through `replaceFileAtomic`, which needs a sibling temp file in the workspace directory. When the workspace root is read-only but DREAMS.md itself is writable (bind-mounted over it), every dream diary write fails with EROFS — including the placeholder entry memory-core appends when narrative generation fails. The MEMORY.md writer already handles this layout by falling back to an in-place write; the DREAMS.md writer did not.

This change catches EACCES/EPERM/EEXIST/EROFS from the atomic replace and falls back to the MEMORY.md writer's `writeExistingMemoryInPlace` — one owner for the in-place recovery instead of a duplicate helper. The fallback re-checks the target identity and revalidates the live mutation authority immediately before the write effects (`assertBeforeMutation`, checked after the preimage read and open), keeps the existing permissions, and restores the preimage at offset zero via `writeFileWindowFully` if the write fails partway, reporting a restore failure instead of silently suppressing it. The maintenance-worker path inherits the fix: it calls `writeDreamsFileAtomic` without a workspace directory.

Re-review follow-up: an authority rejection raised by `assertBeforeMutation` used to fall into the write-recovery path, so a revoked request still performed restore writes (`writeFileWindowFully` + `truncate`) even though no mutation had started. `writeExistingMemoryInPlace` now tracks whether mutation started and lets a pre-mutation rejection escape without entering recovery; the handle is still closed in `finally`. The exact file-mode assertion in the fallback test is now guarded on Windows (`process.platform !== "win32"`), matching the existing permission test in the same file.

## Evidence

Real-behavior proof on Linux, reproducing the reported layout (read-only workspace mount + writable bind-mounted DREAMS.md, via `unshare -rm`):
- On base: `writeDreamsFileAtomic` fails with `EROFS: read-only file system, open '.../DREAMS.md.dreams.<id>.tmp'` — sibling temp-file creation in `replace-file.js`.
- With this fix: the same call succeeds and DREAMS.md contains the new content.
- ClawSweeper P1 follow-up: the fallback now carries the captured mutation authority through the shared helper and revalidates it immediately before the write effects; the restore uses `writeFileWindowFully(handle, original, 0)` and throws if the restore itself fails. Both new regression tests are red on the pre-fix code and green with the fix:
  - "rejects a diary update revoked while the fallback prepares its write" — revocation lands during the fallback's awaited open; the write is rejected with "fixture owner revoked" and DREAMS.md is byte-identical.
  - "restores the original diary byte-for-byte when the in-place write fails partway" — injected EFBIG after a 1024-byte partial write, with a short first restore write; the file is restored to the exact original bytes.
- Re-review follow-up (this head): the revoked-rejection regression now also records every `write` / `writeFile` / `truncate` call on the fallback handle and asserts none happened, so the test proves the rejection performs no write or truncation — not just that the final bytes are unchanged. Red on the previous head (the rejected request performed `["write", "truncate"]` through the restore path), green with the fix. The Windows-only mode assertion is guarded the same way the existing permission test guards it.
- Proof note: the authorized-path evidence above is a shipped-entry-point run on the genuinely read-only layout. The revoked-owner rejection is proven at the owning boundary with call-level evidence (no write or truncate effects); a live terminal capture of a revoked owner through the shipped entry point is not supplied, because revocation can only be injected at that boundary in this environment.
- Fallback suite ("dreams file publication on an unwritable parent", 6 tests: truncation, backfill publication, non-permission failures, missing file, plus the two above) passes; it forces EROFS by rejecting temp-file creation, so it runs as root too.
- Focused tests: `dreaming-dreams-file.test.ts` 34 passed; `short-term-promotion-memory-write.test.ts` 8 passed, 3 skipped (root-gated read-only cases); `memory-mutation-authority.test.ts` 11 passed.
- Gates: test-lines ratchet — the allocation is now exactly the +168 net test-line delta (`config/test-lines-allocations/196508-dreams-inplace-authority.txt`). The earlier 189 grant failed CI: at the CI base main is under its own test-line ceiling, so the ratchet's allocation-credit check caps the grant at the delta. Verified by replaying check-test-lines-ratchet on the merge tree against current main 3d6699cb9 (total 6,636,625; ceiling 6,636,642; slack 17). Line-cap ratchet OK, oxfmt clean, oxlint 0 warnings/errors, tsgo extensions and extensions-test lanes clean.

issue.body:
Fixes #196475

## What Problem This Solves

Once the active transcript grows past `maxActiveTranscriptBytes`, the host shows the `context_bounded` notice ("⚠️ Continuing with bounded recent context…") on what looks like every turn — even when the context engine (lossless-claw in the report) assembles the prompt well within budget. The transcript is large because of image tool results (computer-use screenshots), not model-visible history, and compaction cannot shrink those bytes, so the byte latch stays set and the warning repeats. Users read it as memory loss, although nothing was actually omitted from the model's view beyond the normal summaries.

Root cause: the notice was driven by the latched stored-transcript byte count (`transcriptByteCompactionLatch`), not by what the turn actually assembled. A fitting engine assembly still triggered the warning.

## What Changed

- `src/context-engine/bounded-context.ts`: `boundContextEngineAssembly` records `hostOmittedMessages` (the count of messages the host byte bound dropped) on the result. A fitting assembly leaves it absent, so callers can distinguish it from a truncated one.
- `src/context-engine/types.ts`: `AssembleResult` gains optional `hostOmittedMessages` (host-set only; engines never set it).
- `src/agents/harness/context-engine-lifecycle.ts`: the prepared prompt carries `contextBounded`, true only when `(hostOmittedMessages ?? 0) > 0`.
- `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-history-prepare.ts`: the `context_bounded` omission warning is emitted from the confirmed assembly outcome (`prepared.contextBounded`, and not on settled-turn finalization), via the advisory `onAgentEvent` observer. An observer failure is logged and never aborts the turn.
- `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-memory.ts`: the three byte-latch paths no longer notify `context_bounded` from the latch alone (the latched notice, the over-threshold early return, and the completion notice, which now passes `false` for the bounded flag).
- `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-event-handler.ts`: the run event handler delivers the `context_bounded` warning once per turn. A byte-bounded turn that retries after a provider error re-prepares history per attempt, so the event arrives once per attempt; the handler (one instance per turn) now dedupes it so the turn observer sees it once. Follow-up to @nithishreddy5771's retry edge-case review on head 754f263e.
- `docs/concepts/compaction.md`: documents that the notice follows the turn's actual assembled context, not the stored byte count alone.
- `config/test-lines-allocations/196475-context-bounded-notice.txt`: +140 allocation covering the net test-line growth.

Scope note: this fixes the repeating notice (the first bullet under "Expected" in #196475). Measuring only the post-`/new` segment after a reset (the second bullet) is not part of this change.

## Evidence

- New regression tests, all passing:
  - `attempt-history-prepare.test.ts`: "emits a bounded-context notice only when host bounding omits history" (`contextBounded` true, exactly one `compaction`/`context_bounded` event) and "emits no bounded-context notice when the engine assembly fits" (`contextBounded` false, no event).
  - `context-engine-lifecycle.test.ts`: a fitting custom-engine assembly reports `contextBounded` false; a failed-engine fallback assembly reports `contextBounded` true; the existing bounded-assembly test now also asserts `contextBounded` true.
  - `bounded-context.test.ts`: `hostOmittedMessages` equals the omitted count, and a fitting assembly leaves it `undefined`.
  - `agent-runner-execution-compaction.test.ts`: "delivers the context_bounded warning once per turn across retries" — two `context_bounded` events in one turn (simulating two attempts) deliver the notice exactly once. Red on base: with the handler fix reverted the test fails (notice delivered twice); green with the fix. Full file: 13/13 passed.
- Red on base: the new tests assert the new `contextBounded` / `hostOmittedMessages` fields, which do not exist on the unmodified base, so they cannot pass there (verified by reading the base files; the fields are introduced by this change).
- Vitest: all 6 changed test files passed — `bounded-context.test.ts`, `context-engine-lifecycle.test.ts` (24 tests), `attempt-history-prepare.test.ts`, `agent-runner-memory.test.ts`, `agent-runner-memory.byte-preflight.test.ts` — 5 shards passed in 378.60s; plus `agent-runner-execution-compaction.test.ts` 13/13 passed.
- tsgo core (`tsconfig.core.json`): exit 0 with the retry fix included; the 22 core test shards passed on the prior head.
- oxlint: 0 warnings and 0 errors on the 12 changed TypeScript files. oxfmt `--check`: clean. Docs formatting check: clean (1422 files).
- Test-lines ratchet: net test growth is +140 lines, covered by the new allocation file (+140); local ratchet run: "Test lines OK: 6617953; ceiling: 6617953; slack: 0". Line-cap ratchet: no changed source file grows past its cap (`agent-runner-memory.ts` is net +0 lines).
- Upstream check: none of the 14 changed files were touched on upstream main after the base (`46589542f`), so this branch applies cleanly.

## Not verified

- No live Gateway end-to-end run: this host has no systemd user bus / live session, and no real macOS + Telegram + lossless-claw session to reproduce the reporter's setup. The fix is validated by unit/regression tests at the assembly boundary.
- The pre-commit hook could not run locally (`pnpm` is not installed on this host; the hook fails with `spawn pnpm ENOENT`). The equivalent checks (oxlint, oxfmt, vitest, tsgo shards) were run directly instead.

Closes #193828

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Android Threads → Archived loads only the first 200 archived conversations with no way to browse further pages. The controller parsed the response's pagination metadata and then cleared it for archived results, `loadMoreSessions` refused the archived scope outright, and the archive screen offered no Load More affordance — so the loaded window was silently incomplete and sorting only reordered it.

## User Impact

User impact: with more than 200 archived conversations, the archive screen shows a Load More action with the same loading and failure states the sidebar already uses; continuing loads subsequent archived pages in scope, a failed continuation keeps the loaded rows and offers a retry, and a same-scope refresh preserves rows already loaded beyond the first window instead of pulling the view back to page one. Searching still finds conversations outside the loaded window. The Recent filter in the same screen gains the same Load More affordance when its roster reports more pages, so both scopes behave consistently.

## Why This Change Was Made

`applySessions` kept continuation state only for non-archived results (`if (archived) clearSessionRosterPaging()`), so archived responses discarded `nextOffset`/`hasMore` even though the Gateway already reports them. `loadMoreSessions` also hard-refused when `sessionsListArchived` was set, and its continuation request hardcoded the non-archived scope. Archived pages now keep the same continuation state as the recent roster, the continuation passes `archived = sessionsListArchived`, and the window-refresh path no longer exempts the archive from preserving already-loaded members (`fetchSessionsForCurrentWindow`'s `preserveWindow` guard). The Sessions screen collects the existing roster paging flows and renders the sidebar's Load More row, loading state, and failure caption when the current roster reports more pages.

## Evidence

- New regression `archivedRosterPagesKeepTheirScopeAndRetainLoadedRows` in `ChatControllerCatalogTest.kt`: a 200-row archived refresh reports no more pages; the same request with 201 rows keeps `sessionRosterHasMore` set; a failing continuation returns false, keeps the 200 loaded rows and surfaces `sessionRosterLoadFailed`; a retry loads offset 200, keeps every row `archived == true`, and exhausts paging; a same-scope refresh preserves all 201 loaded rows.
- Red/green: with the production change stashed on this exact commit's base, the new test fails on unmodified `main` (`sessionRosterHasMore` stays false after the 201-row archived refresh — the cleared paging state this PR restores); with the change applied the whole file passes 11/11 (`:app:testPlayDebugUnitTest`, Gradle 9.7.1, Java 21).

The paging slot now belongs to the listed scope: `loadMoreSessions` takes the caller's scope and refuses a stale listing, so an archive left listed cannot page hidden archived rows into the recent sidebar (the sidebar also hides its Load More row while the archive is listed, and the Threads screen shows the row only on the Recent and Archived tabs of the listed scope). Closes #193529

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw plugins uninstall` keeps a home-relative `plugins.load.paths` entry (the documented `~/...` form) after removing a linked plugin, so the "uninstalled" plugin stays discoverable and shows up in `plugins list` as `disabled` / `record-missing`. The same path written absolute is removed correctly.

## User Impact

User impact: uninstalling (and package update/replace ownership checks for) a plugin whose load path uses the documented `~/...` form now removes that path like the absolute form does, so uninstalled plugins stop reappearing in `plugins list`.

## Why This Change Was Made

`loadPathMatchesInstallPath` in `src/plugins/uninstall-package-config.ts` compared paths without home expansion: `resolveRealpathOrAbsolute("~/plugins/demo")` treats `~` as a literal directory and falls back to `path.resolve(cwd, ...)`, which never equals the absolute install path. Discovery (`src/plugins/discovery.ts`) and the update helpers (`buildLoadPathHelpers` in `src/plugins/update-config.ts`) resolve load paths through `resolveUserPath`, so the uninstall/package-update comparison was the one that disagreed. Both sides of the comparison now expand through `resolveUserPath` before the canonical comparison, covering the three shared consumers (`removePluginInstallOwnerFromConfig`, `removePluginRuntimePolicyFromConfig`, `hasMatchingPluginLoadPath`).

## Evidence

- Regression tests in the new sibling file `src/plugins/uninstall-load-path-matching.test.ts` (uninstall.test.ts is over the line-cap ratchet, so the hook forbids growing it): a `~/plugin` load path resolving to the install path is removed with `loadPath` action reported; home-relative paths owned by other plugins are kept. `node scripts/test-projects.mts src/plugins/uninstall-load-path-matching.test.ts src/plugins/uninstall.test.ts` — 78/78 passing, plus consumer suites `plugin-package-update.test.ts` (9), `management-service.uninstall-ownership.test.ts` (14), `management-uninstall.source-cleanup.test.ts` (19), and `plugins-local-state.test.ts` (19) all passing.
- `pnpm check:changed`: typecheck core, typecheck core tests, lint core changed files, format, and all boundary guards pass. The only red lane is the pre-existing `deadcode` scan flagging `extensions/google/provider-policy.ts: normalizeGoogleServiceTier` and `scripts/e2e/lib/upgrade-survivor/config-recipe.mts: resolveScenarioConfigSteps` — exports in files this PR does not touch.
- The 49 added test lines have a matching allocation in `config/test-lines-allocations/plugins-uninstall-tilde-load-path.txt`.


## Real CLI behavior proof (head 9dbacc529f6c)

Run from source (`node --import tsx src/entry.ts`) with isolated `HOME` (fixture plugin at `~/plugins/demo-tilde`), isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, and a fresh config. Fixture plugin: minimal `openclaw.plugin.json` + `package.json` + `index.js`.

**Unpatched `origin/main` (480d5030538)** — after `plugins install --link --force --accept-capabilities ~/plugins/demo-tilde`, config `plugins.load.paths = ["~/plugins/demo-tilde", "/opt/shared-tools/plugin"]`:

```
$ openclaw plugins uninstall demo-tilde --force
Uninstalled plugin "demo-tilde". Removed: install record.
# config after: plugins.load.paths = ["~/plugins/demo-tilde", "/opt/shared-tools/plugin"]
#   → the home-relative path SURVIVES (the bug); uninstall kept the plugin discoverable
```

**This patch, identical steps and inputs:**

```
$ openclaw plugins install --link --force --accept-capabilities '~/plugins/demo-tilde'
exit=0  Linked plugin path: ~/plugins/demo-tilde
$ openclaw plugins uninstall demo-tilde --force
exit=0  Uninstalled plugin "demo-tilde". Removed: install record, load path.
# config after: plugins.load.paths = ["/opt/shared-tools/plugin"]
#   → home-relative path removed; unrelated absolute path and agents config preserved
```

**Package-update consumer (`hasMatchingPluginLoadPath` in `plugin-package-update.ts`)** — a real git-source plugin installed from a local two-tag repo, config `plugins.load.paths = ["~/.openclaw/state/git/git-c30035d65a579ddc/repo", "~/plugins/demo-tilde"]` (home-relative forms):

```
$ openclaw plugins update demo-git
exit=0  demo-git already at 1.0.0.
        Updates saved; they will load on the next Gateway start.
# config after: both home-relative load paths preserved verbatim; agents config preserved
```

**Data-model compatibility:** every run above started from or produced a config mixing home-relative and absolute load-path forms; installs, the update, and the uninstall all loaded the pre-existing config, preserved unrelated entries, and left the stored spellings unchanged. ## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a provider 401 that states its own credential recovery (OpenCode `api_key_expired`: "Create a new API key in OpenCode Console. issue.body:
Closes #193813

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: finishing a voice note in a nearly full attachment draft destroys the recording. `addVoiceNoteAttachment` deleted the capture file in an unconditional `defer`, the aggregate-budget rejection from `stageAttachment` was ignored, and the recorder returned to idle — so removing another attachment could not recover the note, and the only copy of the recording was gone.

## User Impact

User impact: a capture the aggregate budget rejects is now retained with its file and surfaced in the composer as a retry/discard row. Removing an attachment retries it automatically (the issue's recovery case), the Retry button re-stages against the current budget, and Discard deletes the file explicitly. Successful staging still removes the temporary file, and the upload limit itself is unchanged. Recordings over the per-note 5 MB limit or unreadable files are still discarded, since no amount of freed budget can admit them.

## Why This Change Was Made

The recorder handoff now retains a capture the draft cannot admit instead of destroying it. The retained note (`OpenClawRetainedVoiceNote`, module-internal: recording URL, duration, and the exact localized rejection message captured at retention time) belongs to the draft that recorded it:

- The draft pins its owner (`isAttachmentOwnerPinned`, send paths, and programmatic `send()`) until the note is staged or discarded, so a pending session switch cannot strand it; `syncSession` completes after the note resolves.
- Removing an attachment retries staging synchronously through the MainActor retry guard; the voice-note button is disabled while a note is retained, so there is never more than one retained capture and no supersession races.
- Retry validity is identity-based (`retainedVoiceNote?.recording == recording` re-checked after every await), so a discarded note's bytes cannot reappear; the rejection banner is cleared by exact message match, which is locale-safe.
- Discard deletes the file explicitly; staged transfers delete it; a fresh `readAndStageVoiceNote` failure with a superseded or cleared retention leaves the draft untouched.

## Evidence

- Regression tests in `ChatFileAdmissionTests.swift`: the retained note keeps the draft pinned ("Keep this recording with the draft" scenario — pending session switch waits, auto-retry after removal admits the note into the original draft, then the switch completes) and a short-budget retry keeps the note until discard. The parametrized `all staging paths count existing attachment bytes` voice branch pins retention plus explicit-discard deletion; aggregate enforcement stays pinned; the success/oversize/malformed-duration tests pass against the retained signature.
- Two independent review rounds drove the implementation (a compile-level setter visibility defect, a locale-dependent error-prefix match, and lifecycle/concurrency gaps including discard-retry resurrection and duplicate staging); the final design replaces the generation counter with draft ownership plus identity re-validation, reviewed to confirmation.
- Local gates on this commit: `swiftc -parse` clean on all nine touched Swift files, `scripts/format-swift.sh ios` reports 0/514 files needing formatting, `pnpm native:i18n:verify` passes (inventory carries the new apple-surface strings). This host has Command Line Tools only — no full Xcode — so the SwiftUI SDK macro plugins cannot load and the native build/test gate is the iOS/macOS CI on this PR, consistent with `docs/platforms/mac/dev-setup.md`.

## Current review status

Draft: the repair for the published revision's build failure is pushed as the current head. Remaining before ready, per the review plan: hosted iOS/macOS build lanes on this head, the focused regression suites in CI, and isolated iOS simulator evidence covering recording, rejection, retry, and discard.

issue.body:
Closes #194621

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw doctor --session-sqlite recover` could spend hours at 100% CPU with zero disk writes after the actual recovery work finished — inside the failure-report sanitizer (`collectFailureReportIssues` → `sanitize` → `sanitizeFailureIssueMessage` → `shortenFailureReportPath`) — when a large agent store produced six-figure recorded-issue counts (the reporter's u1 store: 103,317 `historical_transcript_deferred` issues), with the same 103k-entry set sanitized more than once per run.

## User Impact

User impact: recovery reports on large stores render in seconds instead of hours, and the report stays byte-shaped the same (per-issue sanitization rules unchanged). As a side effect of the per-report memoization, an issue's redacted session-key pseudonym is now stable within one report — the same session key gets the same token in its field and message instead of a fresh random token per line, and identical issues share one token across the recorded-evidence and recovery lists.

## Why This Change Was Made

The sanitizer re-split every issue message against every planned/completed move path — an issues × paths workload (103k × tens of thousands of recorded moves) — recomputed each path's shortened form once per issue per path even though it only depends on the target, and repeated the entire pass for the recovery issue list and again in `createSessionSqliteMigrationFailureIssue`'s per-issue map. The path table is now shortened once per target (first occurrence wins, matching the original sequential replacement order), matched with chunked single-pass alternation regexes (a whole-table pattern exceeds the engine's regex size limit at recovery scale), and sanitized messages are memoized by session key and raw message, so repeated passes and identical issues reuse their result. No issues × paths term remains.

## Evidence

- New scale regression `bounds sanitizer work when a recovery records tens of thousands of moves and issues` in `doctor-session-sqlite.failure-reports.test.ts`: a schema-valid manifest with 20,000 recorded issues × 4,000 planned moves renders in ~0.1s (asserted < 60s; the pre-fix sequential scans took minutes to hours at this shape), the report body stays within its 20,000-char bound, and the first recorded issue survives with its code and verbatim path.
- The full file passes 13/13 (`node scripts/test-projects.mts src/commands/doctor-session-sqlite.failure-reports.test.ts`).
- Independent review found no P0/P1 defects and ran a 20,000-case differential fuzz of the old and new sanitizers (prefix-chained tables, regex metacharacters, unicode, duplicates, chunk sizes 1/2/3/500): zero output mismatches. Its findings are applied: the vacuous length-only assertion was replaced with content assertions, the redaction token is now per-report stable and consistent between an issue's field and message, and the memo cache key uses the collision-proof `JSON.stringify` idiom.
- `pnpm check:changed`: all lanes pass except the pre-existing red lanes on current `main` untouched by this diff (`changelog attributions`, and the `dead export scan` flagging `src/gateway/control-ui-availability.ts`). The 54 added test lines have a matching `config/test-lines-allocations/doctor-sanitizer-scale.txt` record (credit = net growth; `Test lines OK` locally).
- Not exercised: a real 2.2 GiB agent store recovery end-to-end; the schema-valid 20k × 4k manifest stands in for the reported shape.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the `openclaw agent` text output path printed only an earlier tool-failure warning payload ("⚠️ Bash failed") and exited 1 when the run then failed on a provider usage limit, so the operator never saw the usage-limit message or its reset time and had to export the session trajectory to find the real cause.

## User Impact

User impact: a failed run's explanation now reaches the terminal. After the payload lines, the CLI prints the response summary (e.g. "You've reached your Codex subscription usage limit. Next reset in 2 hours, …") whenever the run did not succeed and no payload already shows that text; success runs are unchanged, and duplicated text is not printed twice.

## Why This Change Was Made

The text path had two disjoint branches: empty-payload responses print `response.summary` on a non-ok status, but responses with any payload printed only the payload contents and never the summary (`agent-via-gateway.ts`). The failure scenario fills the payload list with the tool-warning and leaves the usage-limit text in the summary. The payload-rendering block moved to a sibling module (`agent-via-gateway-text-output.ts`) — behavior-preserving for the loop — which then prints the summary after the payloads for non-ok statuses ("ok"/"completed" exempt, matching `markAgentRunExitCode`), with a trimmed exact-match dedup so an identical payload is not shown twice.

## Evidence

- Two regressions in `agent-via-gateway.session-id.test.ts`: a failed response carrying a tool-warning payload plus a usage-limit summary prints both lines and exits 1; and a summary already present as a payload prints exactly once. `node scripts/test-projects.mts src/commands/agent-via-gateway.session-id.test.ts src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` — all passing, including the untouched pre-existing suites.

issue.body:
Closes #194303
Related: #194336

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a `/stop` handled while a queued follow-up waited for replay admission mirrors its command exchange (a `command-input:` user row and a `command-reply:` assistant row) into the transcript between selection and admission. Replay admission refused the persisted user turn ("Persisted user turn changed before replay admission"), so the queued message died unanswered — no model call, nothing retries it — and on 2026.10.10 it surfaced as "Session transcript keyed user is outside the current turn" after fallback walking.

## User Impact

User impact: a queued follow-up now survives a `/stop` that lands in its admission race: the existing refresh-once re-admission re-selects across the mirrored exchange and answers the original message without a resend. The exchange rows stay in the transcript as replayable conversation. Newer real user messages still refuse admission (the walk stops on the first non-spanning row and `matchesUser` re-validates equality), and genuine faults keep their existing failures.

## Why This Change Was Made

`isInterruptedTurnEntry` decides which rows span the interrupted turn's boundary. Operational delivery-mirror notices (Workshop, model-fallback) already span it — that is what let #181473's refresh-once re-admit a raced turn. Delivered command exchanges are recorded as replayable conversation, not delivery bookkeeping (`transcript.ts`), yet their `command-input:`/`command-reply:` rows did not span, so the mirrored `/stop` closed the turn and every retry re-refused. Command rows now span the turn like notices; the refresh-once still re-validates message equality and interrupted-ness, and the admit-time anchor pin still rejects wrong-turn replays. Real user turns mint keys from different producers (`${runId}:user`, `channel-user:v1:...`), so no real user row can be mistaken for a command row.

## Review status

The [review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194342#issuecomment-6697524073) asks the area owner to decide whether to let replay cross every mirrored command exchange or only the delayed Stop exchange. #194336 proposes the same broad change. Live proof from a shipped Gateway or channel remains outstanding; this draft preserves the in-process regression while that decision is pending.

## Evidence

- New regression `attempt-session-replay.stop-exchange.test.ts` (registered beside its siblings in `test/vitest/vitest.database-worker-core-paths.mjs`), built from the reporter's reproducer: with no interposed write the follow-up is answered; a Workshop notice replays across once (unchanged #181473 behavior); the `/stop` exchange now also replays across once — persisted follow-up answered (`modelCalls: 1`, `FOLLOWUP_ANSWERED`, no thrown error) with the exchange rows present exactly once — on both the selected-owner and non-selected-reader paths. - `node scripts/test-projects.mts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-session-replay.stop-exchange.test.ts` — 6/6 passing; sibling suites `attempt-session-replay.test.ts`, `attempt-session-replay-cohort.test.ts`, and `commands-plugin.channel-native.test.ts` pass unchanged.

Its test-strength suggestion (explicit `thrown` assertion) is applied.

The 159 added test lines have a matching `config/test-lines-allocations/replay-admission-command-exchange.txt` record; note the `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` lane currently fails for any positive test-line growth because `main` itself is over the ratchet ceiling by inherited debt (measured on `origin/main`: over by 49 with net delta 0), as documented on #194270 as well.

Closes #193534

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw config get/set/unset agents.entries.work...` cannot address an agent entry stored under a mixed-case key (`Work`) even though `openclaw agents list` shows it by its normalized id (`work`). `config get` reports the path valid but unset, `config set` tries to create a second `work` key and is declined with the duplicate-id error, and `config unset` reports the path not found.

## User Impact

User impact: the agent id that `agents list` prints now addresses the stored entry through `config get/set/unset/patch`, and the stored key keeps its spelling. Exact keys still win, hand-edited configs with casing-colliding keys keep their duplicate-id validation error, and ids that differ beyond casing (`work!`, `!!!`) remain unresolvable instead of silently hitting another agent.

## Why This Change Was Made

The config CLI used the `agents.entries.<id>` segment as a literal object key while the schema accepts keys case-insensitively and the runtime identifies entries by normalized id. `resolveStoredAgentsEntryKey` (in `config-cli-roster.ts`) rewrites the key segment to its stored spelling when the requested key is absent and exactly one stored key differs only by casing. The mutation runner resolves stored casing before checking whether a conditional write would redirect. If it would, the command rejects the write and leaves the config untouched. `config get` resolves the stored key before lookup while schema diagnostics use the authored path. A delete-then-write across casings in one patch still renames, because the second write only resolves when the stored key is gone.

## Evidence

- Integration tests in `src/cli/config-cli.roster.integration.test.ts`: `set`/`get`/`unset` through `agents.entries.work...` edit the stored `Work` entry in place (key spelling preserved, no duplicate id); `unset` of ids that differ beyond casing (`agents.entries["!!!"].name`, `agents.entries.work!.name`) still fails with the path-not-found error and leaves the config untouched. `node scripts/test-projects.mts src/cli/config-cli.roster.integration.test.ts` — 23/23 passing.
- Sibling suites: `config-cli.test.ts` (14), `config-cli.integration.test.ts` (25), `config-cli-input.test.ts` + `config-cli-path.test.ts` + `config-cli-runner.supplied-intent.test.ts` (91 combined) all passing.

- The gateway `agents.delete` sibling gap (#190496) is intentionally untouched; this PR scopes the fix to the config CLI surfaces named in the issue.


## Real CLI behavior proof

Run from source (`node --import tsx src/entry.ts`) with isolated `HOME`, `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` holding `{"agents":{"ownership":"explicit","entries":{"main":{},"Work":{"name":"Work Agent"}}}}`.

```
$ openclaw config get agents.entries.work.name
Config path is valid but unset: agents.entries.work.name. ...
$ openclaw config set agents.entries.work.name '"Renamed"' --strict-json
Config change declined. No settings were saved.
Config validation failed: agents.entries.work: agents.entries keys "Work" and "work" resolve to the same agent id "work"; ...
$ openclaw config unset agents.entries.work.name
Config path not found: agents.entries.work.name. Nothing was changed.
# saved agents.entries: {"main":{},"Work":{"name":"Work Agent"}}  (unchanged)
```

```
Work Agent
$ openclaw config set agents.entries.work.name '"Renamed"' --strict-json
Updated agents.entries.work.name. Change will apply without restarting the gateway.

$ openclaw config unset agents.entries.work.name

$ openclaw config set agents.entries.work.name '"Renamed"' --strict-json --expect-current-json '"Work Agent"'
```

comment.body:
Root-cause trace (source inspection on current main, no runtime repro — the reporter's device trace stands):

The photo never reaches the transcript because the gateway's shared user-turn assembly deliberately skips media persistence for ACP bridge clients. In `src/gateway/server-methods/chat-send-user-turn.ts`, `prepareChatSendUserTurn` short-circuits `persistInboundImagesForTranscript` when `isAcpBridgeClient(client)` is true, so `UserTurnInput.media` / `mediaImageLayout` stay empty and the persisted user message carries no `media://inbound/…` facts (`src/sessions/user-turn-transcript.metadata.ts` writes `__openclaw.media` only when non-empty). The skip is test-protected: `"leaves ACP bridge user persistence to the agent runtime"` in `src/gateway/server-methods/chat.directive-tags.test.ts` asserts `savedMediaCalls` stays empty for the ACP client identity (`{id: CLI, mode: CLI, displayName: "ACP", version: "acp"}`, matched by `isAcpBridgeClient` in `chat-origin-routing.ts`).

Everything upstream of that skip is shared and working: the ACP translator converts image blocks to attachments (`src/acp/event-mapper.ts`), the gateway parses/offloads them identically to Control UI uploads (`src/gateway/chat-attachments.ts`), and the acpx harness forwards them to the model (`extensions/acpx/src/harness-attempt.ts`, which is why the assistant can read the photo). The replay ledger records the raw prompt independently (`src/acp/translator.session-updates.ts`), which is why `acp_replay_events` has the image while the transcript does not.

So the fix is a design decision between two owners, not a missing conversion:

1. **Gateway**: remove the ACP skip so ACP images persist exactly like Control UI uploads (smallest change, but it reverses the documented contract above — the reason for the skip is unrecorded since the July refactor that introduced it).
2. **acpx harness**: persist media at approval time (`persistApproved` in `extensions/acpx/src/harness-attempt.ts`), which needs the harness to gain media-store custody (save bytes, mint `media://inbound/` refs, attach facts to the staged input) — new ownership surface in the extension.
3. Keep current behavior (photos recoverable only via the replay ledger).

Happy to implement whichever shape maintainers prefer; option 1 is the well-contained one but needs the contract change acknowledged.

Fixes: `openclaw config get/set/unset agents.entries.work...` cannot address an agent entry stored under a mixed-case key (`Work`) even though `openclaw agents list` shows it by its normalized id (`work`). `config get` reports the path valid but unset, `config set` tries to create a second `work` key and is declined with the duplicate-id error, and `config unset` reports the path not found.

User impact: the agent id that `agents list` prints now addresses the stored entry through `config get/set/unset/patch`, and the stored key keeps its spelling. issue.body:
Closes #193528

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a Telegram reply containing a numbered list with nested bullets arrives with a blank line between every numbered item and its own sub-bullets, so the sub-bullets visually detach from their parent. This hits the default Telegram text path (`richMessages` unset) for replies and `openclaw message send`.

## User Impact

User impact: `1. Install\n   - run setup\n   - check version\n2. Configure` renders as one ordered list with its sub-bullets attached to each item; bullet blocks that start a new numbered section keep their separating blank line, so existing section spacing is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

`preserveTelegramListBoundarySpacing` inserted the boundary whenever a numbered line followed a bullet line at the same or deeper indent. When the bullet is nested inside an ordered item and the numbered line is the next sibling of that same list, the inserted blank line sits between two items of one list, so markdown-it marks the whole ordered list loose and renders a paragraph gap after every item with nested content. The pass now skips the boundary when the nearest preceding line at the numbered line's indent is an ordered item with the same delimiter and the bullet sits at or past that item's content column (CommonMark already nests it). Shallow bullet blocks (indent below the content column), differing delimiters, blank-line-adjacent cases, and code regions keep the previous behavior.

## Evidence

- Regression tests in `extensions/telegram/src/format.test.ts`: the nested-sibling case (both `.` and `)` delimiters) renders `1. Install\n  • run setup\n  • check version\n2. Configure\n  • edit config\n3. Start` with no gaps; a shallow bullet block (`10. Install\n - run setup\n11. ## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: skills that embed a shared boilerplate section in their SKILL.md body all render that section's heading as their title in the composer skill picker, so distinct skills can appear with identical labels.

## User Impact

User impact: a skill's picker title now comes from a heading that opens the skill's own body — the SKILL.md convention — instead of the first `#` heading found anywhere in the body. Skills that embed a shared reference section keep distinct labels. This changes title selection for skills whose first heading follows introductory prose; that policy requires maintainer review.

## Why This Change Was Made

`resolveSkillDisplayName` matched the first ATX `#` heading anywhere in the body (`/m` flag) and used the frontmatter `name` only when the body had no heading at all. The Agent Skills spec treats frontmatter `name` as the skill identity, and a heading buried in the body is ordinary prose that often belongs to embedded shared content — in the reporter's install, the embedded spec's `# AI-First Note Rules` heading sits at the end of 47 of 49 skills and titles all of them.

The display title now requires the heading to open the body (after leading blank lines). Later headings fall back to the skill's identity: the frontmatter `name`, then the humanized directory name. Skills whose body starts with their own title — including every bundled and custodian skill and the pinned library flow, which asserts heading-derived display titles for such skills — keep the exact display they have today. Anchoring to the body opening preserves the deliberate heading-title design (the library flow's "keeps the heading separate from the selected command identity" behavior) while removing the boilerplate pollution the issue reports.

## What does this PR do?

The lifecycle guard's segment splitter (`_split_segments`) treated `<(` / `>(` the same way it treats control operators like `;` and `&&`: everything after the closing parenthesis started a new command segment. In `diff <(echo a) /dev/null` the operand `/dev/null` was therefore walked as the next command's executable; a character device fails the regular-file check, and the guard's fail-closed policy then blocked the whole read-only command.

This PR rewrites `_split_segments` to be process-substitution-aware: a bare `<`/`>` immediately followed by `(` opens a substitution, and the substitution is grouped by balanced parenthesis depth (nesting and arithmetic expansions included). The interior is yielded as its own segment(s) so it is still scanned — it does execute — while tokens after the closing `)` remain operands of the outer run. An unterminated substitution still has its interior scanned. The rebuild mode (`keep_controls=True`) is unchanged and preserves the original tokens exactly.

- **Receiver**: `hermes_cli/gateway_client.py:67-82` — `_bounded_error_data` deliberately preserves lists of ≤ 16 short strings (lines 80-81), so `data.fields` arrives intact on `GatewayRPCError.data`.
- **Last hop**: `hermes_cli/cli_chat_error_copy.py:36-54` — `refusal_text` (verified on current `origin/main` via `gh api`; the read is at lines 49-54) reads only the singular `data.get('field')`/`data.get('detail')` (line 51). `fields` is silently dropped, the copy falls to `str(error)` = the bare `invalid_params`, and `agent_init_failure_message` (same file, lines 87-96) wraps that into the `locales/en.yaml:3296` `cli.error.agent_init_failed` copy — misleading, provider-facing text for a policy refusal.

issue.body:
## What does this PR do?

When `auxiliary.vision` is pinned to a provider that cannot be resolved, the vision chain correctly falls back to the auto backends — but it carried the **pinned task's model** into the fallback, pairing a model id from one vendor with another vendor's endpoint. The request then dies upstream (`400 <model> is not a valid model ID`) even though the log line directly above shows the correct autodetected model being computed and then discarded.

The fallback now walks `_vision_auto_route` directly instead of re-entering `resolve_vision_provider_client(provider="auto", model=resolved_model, ...)`. The re-entry was the bug: `resolve_vision_provider_client` re-resolves the task config, so its `_resolve_task_provider_model` call resurrects `auxiliary.vision.model` from config even when the caller passes `model=None`. `_vision_auto_route` is the same chain minus that config re-read, and it matches the text branch's existing contract (`_get_cached_client("auto", ..., task=task)` — "model=None so each provider uses its own default").

A provider that *does* resolve keeps its pinned model; only the unavailable-provider fallback drops it.

## Related Issue

Fixes #145182

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `agent/auxiliary_client.py` — `_resolve_call_client`, vision branch: the unavailable-provider fallback now calls `_vision_auto_route(_normalize_main_runtime(main_runtime), None, None, async_mode)` so the auto chain resolves the model for the endpoint it actually picked.
- `tests/agent/test_auxiliary_vision_fallback_model.py` — new regression tests:
  - pinned provider unresolvable + pinned model → resolved route carries the **autodetected** model, not the pinned one;
  - auto chain returning no default still never leaks the pinned model;
  - guard: a pinned provider that resolves keeps the pinned model.

## How to Test

1. `config.yaml`:
   ```yaml
   model:
     provider: openrouter
     default: deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017
   auxiliary:
     vision:
       provider: custom:does-not-exist   # unresolvable
       model: Qwen3.5-9B-oQ4e-mtp        # a model that only exists on that local endpoint
   ```
2. Trigger any auxiliary vision call (e.g. `vision_analyze`, or `call_llm(task="vision", ...)`). Before the fix the route resolves to `openrouter` + `Qwen3.5-9B-oQ4e-mtp` and the request 400s; after the fix it resolves to `openrouter` + the main provider's model.
3. `HERMES_PYTHON=<venv python> scripts/run_tests.sh tests/agent/test_auxiliary_vision_fallback_model.py` — 3 passed on this branch; the first two fail on unmodified `main` (red/green confirmed).

issue.body:
## Summary

Selecting an image model in WebUI can implicitly save `tools.media.image.quality: ""` (the model picker writes an empty quality when the reader picks a model without choosing one), and `effective_quality()` treated any explicitly-present quality key as authoritative, so that empty string outranked the tool call's own request. The `if quality:` sites then dropped the empty value from the outbound request, so a call asking for `quality: "high"` went out with no quality at all. The fix is one condition: an empty Settings value is the section's "no quality named" (the schema's own default, per the config docstring and the tool schema's "Quality used only when Settings has no quality"), so it falls through to the request; a quality actually named in Settings still wins over the call's. The configured model keeps its documented precedence over the requested model, unchanged.

issue.body:
Closes #184724

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: skills that embed a shared boilerplate section in their SKILL.md body all render that section's heading as their title in the composer skill picker, so distinct skills can appear with identical labels.

## User Impact

User impact: a skill's picker title now comes from a heading that opens the skill's own body — the SKILL.md convention — instead of the first `#` heading found anywhere in the body. Skills that embed a shared reference section keep distinct labels. This changes title selection for skills whose first heading follows introductory prose; that policy requires maintainer review.

## Why This Change Was Made

`resolveSkillDisplayName` matched the first ATX `#` heading anywhere in the body (`/m` flag) and used the frontmatter `name` only when the body had no heading at all. The Agent Skills spec treats frontmatter `name` as the skill identity, and a heading buried in the body is ordinary prose that often belongs to embedded shared content — in the reporter's install, the embedded spec's `# AI-First Note Rules` heading sits at the end of 47 of 49 skills and titles all of them.

The display title now requires the heading to open the body (after leading blank lines). Later headings fall back to the skill's identity: the frontmatter `name`, then the humanized directory name. Skills whose body starts with their own title — including every bundled and custodian skill and the pinned library flow, which asserts heading-derived display titles for such skills — keep the exact display they have today. Anchoring to the body opening preserves the deliberate heading-title design (the library flow's "keeps the heading separate from the selected command identity" behavior) while removing the boilerplate pollution the issue reports.

## Evidence

- New unit tests in `src/skills/loading/skill-materializer.test.ts`. Against unpatched `origin/main`, exactly the boilerplate case fails (title came out as "AI-First Note Rules" from the embedded section at the end of the body); with the fix all four cases pass: boilerplate heading ignored ("Obsidian Save" from the frontmatter name), body-opening heading kept ("Short Description"), title heading after leading blank lines kept, and the humanized fallback without any heading.
- Every existing assertion is unchanged: `skills.test.ts` heading-derived display, `library/service.test.ts` "keeps the heading separate from the selected command identity" (heading case still renders "Friendly Title"), and the bundled/custodian skills whose bodies open with their titles.
- `pnpm test` passes on all suites exercising the materializer and its consumers: `src/skills/loading/`, `src/skills/library/`, `src/skills/discovery/`, skills runtime resources, embedded agent runner skill-runtime suites, and the CLI live session registry. The one red file, `workspace-skill-sync.runtime.test.ts` ("preserving unchanged destinations"), fails identically on unpatched `origin/main` on this machine (macOS temp-dir ENOENT) and is untouched by this PR.
- `pnpm check:changed`: typecheck core, typecheck core tests, lint, formatting, and the guard lanes pass. The only red lane is the pre-existing `deadcode` unused-export scan, which flags three exports in files this PR does not touch (`src/infra/sqlite-worker-operation-settlement.ts`, `src/boards/board-store.fixtures.test-support.ts`, `src/commands/cleanup-command.test-support.ts`); no path owned by this PR appears in its output.


**Follow-up:** Leading blank lines are now skipped without stripping indentation from the first content line, so an indented code block is not treated as a title. issue.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

Human-authored webchat messages can be persisted to a session transcript without the sender ever being recorded as a session participant. Those sessions then never appear in that person's "Involving me" list (`sessions.list` `relationship: "involving"`).

`chat.send` writes the user message, including `senderIdentity`, to the transcript at request time. It only *prepares* the participant on the in-memory context (`prepareSessionParticipantInput`, `src/gateway/server-methods/chat-send-user-turn.ts`). The durable participant row is written much later, in `initSessionState` (`src/auto-reply/reply/session.ts`, `recordAcceptedSessionParticipantInput`, gated by `!isSystemEvent && !isInterSession`). Any accepted message whose dispatch never reaches `initSessionState` therefore leaves an authored transcript message with no participant record.

We observed two ways that happens:

1. **Restart recovery takes over a turn that never started.** The turn was accepted and persisted, but it stalled in reply initialization while the gateway was heavily backlogged after a restart. Main-session restart recovery then selected the session (`decision=started reason=dispatch_started`, `sourceRunId` = the user's run) and answered with an `internal_system` continuation turn. The original run never emitted `session.started`, and the recovery turn is a system turn, so the participant is skipped.
2. **A follow-up is rejected at admission.** The message is persisted, then the dispatch is skipped with `reason: "reply-operation-active"` after waiting in `reply.admit_pre_dispatch`. No participant is recorded.

The "Involving me" filter (`session-row-selection.ts` → `prepareInvolvements`) only considers the owner, `participants` and mentions, so the author is invisible even though their messages, with verified profile IDs, are in the transcript.

### Steps to reproduce

Observed on a production Team gateway, not yet reduced to a minimal repro:

1. User A owns a shared dashboard session. User B has never prompted it.
2. Restart the gateway while many main sessions have interrupted work, so post-restart recovery and reply initialization are slow. We saw `slow chat send … replyInitialization=` values from 55s to more than 900s, plus provider rate limits.
3. User B sends a webchat message to A's session. `chat.send` acks and the message is persisted, but the turn does not start.
4. Main-session restart recovery dispatches a continuation for that session, using B's run as `sourceRunId`, and the continuation answers B's question.
5. User B sends more messages while the recovery turn is active. They are persisted and then skipped with `reply-operation-active`.
6. Run `sessions.list` with `relationship: "involving"` as User B. The session is missing, and the session's `participants` contain only A, plus anyone else whose turn completed normally.

A deterministic repro probably only needs: accept a `chat.send` turn, block it before `initSessionState`, and resolve it through restart recovery or an admission skip. Then assert that `session_participants` lacks the sender.

### Expected behavior

A human whose authored message is durably accepted into a session's transcript is recorded as a session participant, whether the turn is later completed normally, completed by restart recovery, queued, or skipped because another reply operation is active.

### Actual behavior

The message shows the correct `senderId`/`senderIdentity` in the transcript, but the session's `participants` never include that profile. "Involving me" omits the session indefinitely, until that user gets a turn that runs normally or is @mentioned.

### OpenClaw version

2026.10.7 (3b3efe9). The same recording placement is still present in b4e7ddf.

### Operating system

Linux 7.0.0-38-generic x64 (Ubuntu host, systemd service)

### Install method

Managed release directory under systemd (`openclaw-gateway.service`)

### Model

openai/gpt-6.1-sol

### Provider / routing chain

openclaw → openai (api-key), fallback openai/gpt-6-astra

### Additional provider/model setup details

Not provider-specific. OpenAI `rate_limit_exceeded` errors during the window contributed to the post-restart backlog, but they aren't the cause of the missing participant.

### Logs

```text
23:06:47 gateway ready                     (after restart; 20 interrupted main sessions marked at 23:05:53)
23:17:24 ⇄ res ✓ chat.send 4326ms runId=<B-run-1>        # user B message persisted
         (no runtime session.started for <B-run-1> in the session trajectory)
23:25:59 transcript message.custom  "OpenClaw admitted a continuation of this request after the Gateway restarted…"
23:26:02 main-session restart recovery candidate {"sourceRunId":"<B-run-1>","decision":"started","reason":"dispatch_started","nextOwner":"main-lane"}
23:26:04 runtime session.started run=<recovery-run>      # provenance internal_system / main_session_restart_recovery
23:26:43 reply-timing outcome=skipped reason=reply-operation-active spans=[reply.admit_pre_dispatch 55233ms]   # B's follow-up
23:28:55 ⇄ res ✓ chat.send runId=<B-run-2>               # same pattern repeats
23:36:15 main-session restart recovery candidate {"sourceRunId":"<B-run-2>","decision":"started","reason":"dispatch_started"}
23:36:38 reply-timing outcome=skipped reason=reply-operation-active spans=[reply.admit_pre_dispatch 34720ms]
```

No production gateway restart happened between 23:06:47 and the events above. Recovery adopted runs that were accepted *after* the boot.

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

issue.body:
Addresses the "Pre-update config snapshot is non-atomic" item of #184894.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an update process interrupted mid-write of the `.pre-update` config snapshot can leave a torn rollback point at exactly the moment an update is in flight, losing the only copy of the pre-update config taken outside the rotating `.bak` ring.

## User Impact

User impact: the pre-update rollback point is published by a same-directory rename, avoiding a visible partial replacement during an ordinary interrupted write. This does not establish power-loss durability. An interrupted snapshot attempt cleans up after itself and keeps the prior rollback point usable.

## Why This Change Was Made

`createPreUpdateConfigSnapshot` wrote `${configPath}.pre-update` directly with `flag: "w"`, which truncates the existing file before the new content lands. The fix writes to a unique same-directory temp file (`flag: "wx"`, mode 0600) and renames it onto the snapshot path — the repo's standard temp + rename publication. A failed attempt removes its temp file, and the existing in-process coalescing marker still resets so a later attempt can retry.

## Evidence

- New regression test in `src/config/config.backup-rotation.test.ts` ("keeps the previous snapshot intact when a snapshot attempt fails mid-publication"): red on `origin/main` (the in-place write replaces the previous snapshot, so the older rollback content is lost) and green with the fix (previous snapshot intact, no temp leftovers, retry publishes the newer content).
- The existing suite passes unchanged, including "replaces a preexisting snapshot once per process" and the transient read/write retry test (#105431).
- `pnpm test src/cli/update-cli/` and the touched config suites pass; `pnpm check:changed` passes typecheck core, typecheck core tests, lint, and formatting. The only red lane is the pre-existing `deadcode` unused-export scan, which flags three exports in files this PR does not touch.

issue.title: fix(codex): settled-turn recovery rejects sessions containing a media-only user turn

labels.name: repo-535d150f

issue.body:
Closes #185079

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Codex settled-turn finalization repeatedly fails with `invalid_content` when the session history contains a legitimate media-only user turn — a message persisted with empty text plus ordered `__openclaw.media` facts (for example, a JPEG-only Telegram message) and no upstream-text fallback. The projection validated every earlier message before trimming, so one such historical turn kept rejecting every later finalization context capture on that session.

## User Impact

User impact: a verified historical media-only message no longer invalidates settled-turn recovery. It projects as a bounded, deterministic marker naming the attachment types, and finalization context capture succeeds for sessions that contain one. Empty messages without any well-formed media fact are still rejected, upstream text keeps winning over the placeholder, and current-turn evidence and pairing checks are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

`projectUserMessage` required non-empty text and threw `CodexHistoryRejection("invalid_content")` for a blank user turn. The persisted representation for media-only turns is exactly that shape (empty `content`, media metadata under `message.__openclaw.media` — the documented "media-bearing user turns use ordered `message.__openclaw.media` facts" convention). The payloads themselves are not replayable through the text-oriented recovery projection, so the fix projects a deterministic `[User media attachment unavailable in this context: <types>]` marker — the same approach the projector already uses for image tool results (`[Image tool result: <mime>]`) — capped at the first eight entries with a `+N more` suffix, always inside the existing byte budgets.

## Evidence

- New regression tests in `extensions/codex/src/app-server/settled-turn-projection.test.ts`: against unpatched `origin/main`, exactly the two placeholder-projecting cases fail (media-only turn rejected with `invalid_content`); with the fix all 26 cases pass, including the guards for empty turns without well-formed media facts (still `invalid_content`), upstream-text precedence, and the placeholder cap.
- `pnpm test:extension codex` passes except two `transport-startup.test.ts` cases that fail identically on unpatched `main` on this machine (macOS native process inspection returns a permission error in this environment); the projection suites themselves are fully green.
- `pnpm check:changed` passes typecheck extensions, typecheck extension tests, and lint extension changed files. The only red lane is the pre-existing `deadcode` unused-export scan flagging three exports in files this PR does not touch.


**Remaining proof:** No end-to-end Gateway/Codex recovery run with persisted media-only history has been performed. The regression tests cover the projection boundary; they do not establish the full recovery and finalization flow.

### Summary

Grouped lower-severity findings from a codebase audit (the same audit that produced PR #184858 and issues #184887, #184888, #184889, #184890, #184891, #184892, #184893 for the higher-severity items). Each item is grounded in a direct read of `main` @ `d777ae12` (files unchanged as of `3d7f8fbf`); none was executed end-to-end. Filed together to avoid opening a dozen low-severity issues — happy to see any item split out.

### Steps to reproduce

Each item cites its exact location; all are reachable from shipped production code paths.

- [ ] **Pre-update config snapshot is non-atomic** — `src/config/backup-rotation.ts:215-222` writes the `.pre-update` rollback point with `flag: "w"` (truncate in place). A crash mid-write leaves a torn snapshot at exactly the moment an update is in flight; it self-heals only on the next update attempt. Fix: temp + rename (repo convention).
- [ ] **`withNodeRuntimePath` drops PATH entries when env carries both `Path` and `PATH`** — `node-runtime-env.mjs:86-101` derives `entries` from the alphabetically-first PATH-keyed var only (`"PATH"` sorts before `"Path"`) and writes it to both keys. The Win32 env block is case-insensitive but a JS object is not, so a merged env (service/handoff env assembly) with two differently-cased PATH vars silently loses the second key's directories for every lifecycle child (npm/pnpm child installs, service refresh, recovery respawn).
- [ ] **pnpm-workspace.yaml swap during source updates is not crash-safe and its restore can delete the operator's file** — `src/infra/update-runner-git-commands.ts:199-216`: crash between `rename` and `restoreWorkspace` leaves the tracked file replaced and the original in an orphaned `workspace-original-*` dir that `cleanupGlobalRenameDirs` never cleans (its prefix is `.openclaw-`); if pnpm rewrites the file during the candidate install, the content-equality guard fails and the original is `rm -rf`'d (git-recoverable only because the pre-update clean check guarantees no uncommitted edits).
- [ ] **Read-path auto-recovery can revert an intentional, valid manual edit** — `src/config/io.observe-suspicious.ts:43-45` fires `size-drop-vs-last-good` on any valid read where the file is <50% of the last-known-good baseline (no invalidity requirement); `src/config/io.observe-recovery.ts:342-411` then atomically overwrites `openclaw.json` with `.bak` (edit survives only as `.clobbered.*` + a log warning). Design question: should a read-path heuristic that cannot distinguish "user halved their config" from "something clobbered it" act destructively on a file that still validates?
- [ ] **Ingress claim-conflict loop has no backoff or cap** — `src/channels/message/ingress-queue.ts:299-344` `continue`s on conflict with no sleep/jitter/budget; each iteration costs two worker round-trips, so sustained contention busy-spins the gateway main thread. Lane-key serialization makes this a tail risk.
- [ ] **Recovery backoff sleep ignores abort/shutdown** — `src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue-recovery.ts:1186-1189` awaits a plain `sleep(remainingBackoffMs)` (up to 600s for retryCount ≥ 4) with no AbortSignal. Currently dormant: only reachable when a queued row sets `retryAmbiguousFinalText`, which no bundled caller does today. Fix is `sleepWithAbort(ms, signal)`.
- [ ] **`safeEqualSecret("", "")` returns true** — `src/security/secret-equal.ts:23-26` treats empty-vs-empty as a match. Every current call site guards empty secrets before comparing, but any future call site that skips that guard silently downgrades to "no auth"; consider returning `false` for the empty-empty case.
- [ ] **Multi-root read admission recognizes only 1 of 3 escape-message forms** — `src/agents/agent-tools.read.ts:681-683` matches `/^Path escapes sandbox root \(/` only, while the repo's own complete classifier (`src/agents/sandbox-paths.ts:125-135`) knows three forms and `apply-patch.test.ts:417` shows the symlink form in practice. A `Path resolves outside…`/`Symlink escapes sandbox root…` rejection from the primary root aborts the fallback loop instead of trying additional read roots — false denial (fails closed).
- [ ] **Windows drive-relative tool paths anchor to the process's per-drive CWD** — `src/agents/sandbox-paths.ts:54-64`: `C:temp\file` matches neither `isWindowsDrivePath` (requires a separator) nor `path.win32.isAbsolute`, so it resolves against `process.env['=C:']` rather than the tool cwd; the write lands in a different in-root directory than the documented "relative paths from the workspace directory" contract (`docs/tools/apply-patch.md:47`). Containment still holds.
- [ ] **Hand-authored allowlist entry `{ pattern: "*", argPattern: … }` is silently dead** — `src/infra/exec-command-resolution.ts:334-341,351-366`: the bare-wildcard fast path requires no `argPattern` and the main loop skips `pattern === "*"` unconditionally, while `docs/tools/exec-approvals.md` documents `argPattern` as a general per-entry restriction and `classifyExecAllowlistScope` reports the entry as active. Fails closed, but invisibly to the operator.
- [ ] **apply_patch removed-link matching is case-sensitive on case-insensitive volumes** — `src/agents/apply-patch.ts:477-500` matches later hunk paths against removed links lexically (`path.relative` is case-sensitive) while the module handles case variants elsewhere (`hasCaseVariant`, `:566-580`); a `Delete File: Link` followed by a case-variant re-spelling can false-reject on APFS.
- [ ] **Session-key case folding hardcodes its per-channel exemptions** — `packages/session-url-contract/src/session-key-normalization.ts:117-153` lowercases every peer ID except Signal groups and Matrix rooms; any future channel with structured case-sensitive IDs folds distinct conversations into one session key. Consistent on read and write today, so this is a forward-compatibility note rather than a live collision.

Each item should either be confirmed as an accepted tradeoff (with a comment/naming where missing) or repaired along the lines sketched above.

### Actual behavior

Closes #184724

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: skills that embed a shared boilerplate section in their SKILL.md body all render that section's heading as their title in the composer skill picker, so distinct skills can appear with identical labels.

## User Impact

User impact: a skill's picker title now comes from a heading that opens the skill's own body — the SKILL.md convention — instead of the first `#` heading found anywhere in the body. Skills that embed a shared reference section keep distinct labels. This changes title selection for skills whose first heading follows introductory prose; that policy requires maintainer review.

## Why This Change Was Made

`resolveSkillDisplayName` matched the first ATX `#` heading anywhere in the body (`/m` flag) and used the frontmatter `name` only when the body had no heading at all. The Agent Skills spec treats frontmatter `name` as the skill identity, and a heading buried in the body is ordinary prose that often belongs to embedded shared content — in the reporter's install, the embedded spec's `# AI-First Note Rules` heading sits at the end of 47 of 49 skills and titles all of them.

The display title now requires the heading to open the body (after leading blank lines). Later headings fall back to the skill's identity: the frontmatter `name`, then the humanized directory name. Skills whose body starts with their own title — including every bundled and custodian skill and the pinned library flow, which asserts heading-derived display titles for such skills — keep the exact display they have today. Anchoring to the body opening preserves the deliberate heading-title design (the library flow's "keeps the heading separate from the selected command identity" behavior) while removing the boilerplate pollution the issue reports.

## Evidence

- New unit tests in `src/skills/loading/skill-materializer.test.ts`. Against unpatched `origin/main`, exactly the boilerplate case fails (title came out as "AI-First Note Rules" from the embedded section at the end of the body); with the fix all four cases pass: boilerplate heading ignored ("Obsidian Save" from the frontmatter name), body-opening heading kept ("Short Description"), title heading after leading blank lines kept, and the humanized fallback without any heading.
- Every existing assertion is unchanged: `skills.test.ts` heading-derived display, `library/service.test.ts` "keeps the heading separate from the selected command identity" (heading case still renders "Friendly Title"), and the bundled/custodian skills whose bodies open with their titles.
- `pnpm test` passes on all suites exercising the materializer and its consumers: `src/skills/loading/`, `src/skills/library/`, `src/skills/discovery/`, skills runtime resources, embedded agent runner skill-runtime suites, and the CLI live session registry. The one red file, `workspace-skill-sync.runtime.test.ts` ("preserving unchanged destinations"), fails identically on unpatched `origin/main` on this machine (macOS temp-dir ENOENT) and is untouched by this PR.
- `pnpm check:changed`: typecheck core, typecheck core tests, lint, formatting, and the guard lanes pass.
